'''''Euphorbia lactea''''' is a species of [[Euphorbia|spurge]] native to arid and subtropical regions of [[South Asia]], mainly the [[Indian subcontinent|Indian Subcontinent]].<ref name=rhs>Huxley, A, ed. (1992). ''New RHS Dictionary of Gardening''. {{ISBN|0-333-47494-5}}</ref> [[Common name]]s include '''mottled spurge''',<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 16 January 2018}}</ref> '''frilled fan''', '''elkhorn''',<ref>[https://www.llifle.info/Encyclopedia/SUCCULENTS/Family/Euphorbiaceae/16475/Euphorbia_lactea_f._cristata Euphorbia lactea f. cristata] Llifle.com. Retrieved 1 December 2024.</ref> '''candelabra spurge''',<ref name=grin/> candelabrum tree, candelabra cactus, candelabra plant, '''dragon bones''',<ref name=grin/> '''false cactus''',<ref name=grin/> '''hatrack cactus''',<ref name=grin/> milkstripe euphorbia, mottled candlestick.

==Description==
[[Image:Cactus tronc kourou.jpg|thumb|left|Euphorbia lactea in [[Kourou]], French Guiana.]]
It is an erect [[shrub]] growing up to {{convert|5|m}} tall, with [[succulent]] branches {{convert|3|-|5|cm}} diameter, ridged, with a triangular or rhombic cross-section; the ridges are spiny, with short, permanent spines up to {{convert|5|mm}} long. The [[leaf|leaves]] are small, and quickly [[deciduous]].<ref name=rhs/> 

All parts of the plant contain a [[poison]]ous milky [[latex]], containing several irritating alkaloids, such as [[phorbol]].<ref>Poisonous plants: [http://www.ces.ncsu.edu/depts/hort/consumer/poison/Euphola.htm ''Euphorbia lactea''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090603040336/http://www.ces.ncsu.edu/depts/hort/consumer/poison/Euphola.htm |date=2009-06-03 }}</ref>

==Cultivation==
[[File:Duke euphorbe.jpg|thumb|left|60 year old Euphorbia lactea var. Cristata located at the Duke University greenhouse, Durham, USA.]]
It is used medicinally in [[India]].<ref>Plant of the Week.org [http://www.plantoftheweek.org/week113.shtml ''Euphorbia lactea'']</ref> It is widely grown as an [[ornamental plant]], both in the tropics, and as a [[houseplant]] in temperate regions; a number of [[cultivar]]s have been selected for ornamental use, notably 'Cristata' with frilled branching.<ref name=rhs/><ref>Pacific Island Ecosystems at Risk: [http://www.hear.org/Pier/species/euphorbia_lactea.htm ''Euphorbia lactea'']</ref>
